PASS: QA1 gate 1, round 1: PASS. Audited 3b48ff5 on devteam2/sprint-31, in worktree ../my_little_raccoon-devteam2-sprint-31. The diff covers 6a62fc9..HEAD: the Sprint 31 work in 3562dc3 and 3b48ff5, plus the start bookkeeping.

I re-read the sprint file fresh in the worktree. It differs from main's copy only in the lifecycle-owned status: line. No criterion asserts anything between versions.

R1 Met.
- app/chart/route.ts GET returns NextResponse.redirect with an explicit 307, built from request.url, so it stays on the requesting origin.
- The target comes from chartRedirectTarget in redirect-target.ts: exactly one date value that passes parseDatePageParam goes to datePagePath. Anything else goes to /. params.ts is imported unchanged, with no new export needed. Traced each R7 input:
  - 1969-07-20 goes to /date/1969-07-20.
  - 1700-01-01 and 2100-12-31 go to their own date pages.
  - garbage, 2024-02-30, 1969-7-20 and other malformed values go to /.
  - 1699-12-31, 2101-01-01 and 2200-01-01 go to /.
  - No date and an empty date go to /.
  - A repeated date goes to /, consistent with how /date handles an array.
- The build lists /chart as dynamic.

R2 Met.
- app/chart/page.tsx, actions.ts and chart.module.css are deleted, and so are FlowIndicator.tsx, its test and flow-indicator.module.css.
- grep for FlowIndicator, saveReading and app/chart across app/ and lib/ returns nothing.
- Nothing is orphaned. Every import of the deleted files still has another user: MIN_SUPPORTED_DATE in DatePicker, MAX_SUPPORTED_DATE in DatePicker and generate, CALCULATION_HOUR_UTC in params and ReadingView, and fetchDayEvents and availability in lib/date-page. constellation.ts already lives in app/reading/[id].
- insertReading survives, and its only callers are lib/date-page/cast.ts and lib/readings/insert.test.ts.

R3 Met.
- /reading/[id]/page.tsx drops the FlowIndicator and belowDateBand and passes datePageHref = datePagePath(reading.event_date). event_date is the stored row's, not a request value.
- In ReadingPanel, both links (desktop and mobile) go to datePageHref with the label "Go to this date". A discriminated union makes datePageHref required whenever the link renders. The date page's offerNewChart={false} call is unchanged and still renders no link.
- The "Write the horoscope" and "Try again" branches are untouched, and the 404 and outage paths are untouched.
- actions.ts's missing-id redirect now goes to /.

R4 Met. error.tsx links to / with the label "Go to today". Its comment no longer says "step 1".

R5 Met. The layout.tsx description is rewritten for the date-page app. The README describes /chart as a 307 redirect, and its no-env Local validation list checks the /chart redirects with curl -sI. The health route's comment is updated. A grep of app/ and lib/ source (non-test) for cast a new chart, cast the chart, save this reading, see the full reading and step labels returns nothing.

R6 Met in substance, with one finding against the sprint file itself.
- Nothing under supabase/ changes. params.ts is unchanged.
- app/date/[date]/page.tsx, app/date/[date]/date.module.css and lib/date-page/cast.ts change in COMMENTS ONLY, to remove references to app/chart and saveReading. There is no code, class or behaviour change.
- R2's grep (app/ and lib/, must find nothing) and R6's wording (no change under app/date/ or lib/date-page/ except for the params reuse) cannot both hold. Those files' comments named app/chart. Dev Team satisfied R2 with comment-only edits, which is the right call. For Master Controller: a future sprint pairing a repo-wide grep with a frozen directory should exempt comments explicitly.

R7 Met.
- redirect.test.ts covers every listed target, including both boundaries, malformed, out-of-range and no-date cases, and the route itself: status 307, Location, same origin, and the query string dropped.
- ReadingPanel.test.ts is new. It covers the /reading/[id] link target on both breakpoints, no retired copy and no /chart, the date page rendering no link, and the Write the horoscope and Try again branches.
- Removed tests: FlowIndicator.test.ts only, which exercised only deleted code.
- lib/readings-access-guardrail.test.ts changed one fixture's path and function name, from app/chart/actions.ts and saveReading to app/example/actions.ts and insertOnly, to clear R2's grep. The assertion is the same, and the guardrail module itself is unchanged. That is not a weakening.

Ran these myself in the worktree:
- npm test: 26 files, 291 tests, green.
- typecheck: clean.
- lint: clean.
- build: clean.
The RLS suite is untouched by this diff. I could not run test:rls (no docker in this WSL distro), and CI's rls-tests job covers it.

For Pipeman, informational: the branch forks at 6a62fc9 and does not contain Sprint 30's commits or 5d63055 (the CLAUDE.md block) from main. The two sprints share no source files, so the merge should touch only bookkeeping such as registry.json. Audited tree hash is this branch's HEAD content.

Low, non-blocking: the ReadingPanel prop is still named offerNewChart, a name with no "new chart" behind it anymore. Dev Team kept it deliberately to avoid editing app/date under R6, and documented that. Rename it in a later sprint.

No Human Prerequisites. No test was labelled known-failing.

PASS: QA1 gate 1, round 2: PASS. This is a re-audit after a rebase. The audited tree is HEAD = 361d4536ce9558283de448a0092b7325c6048e6c on devteam2/sprint-31.

Why a re-audit: devteam2/sprint-31 was rebased from 6a62fc9 onto main at ac87051 after my round-1 PASS (recorded at 7bd32f2). That rebase pulled in Sprint 30's migration and tests and the CLAUDE.md Next.js block. The tree therefore differs from the one round 1 audited, and /sprint-ship would correctly refuse it.

Re-derived as follows:
(1) git patch-id --stable is identical for 3562dc3 vs 180ad4a and for 3b48ff5 vs 24d9c2a.
(2) The Sprint 31 code diff, excluding docs/sprints, is byte-identical between 6a62fc9..3b48ff5 and ac87051..361d453.
(3) git diff ac87051 361d453 restricted to supabase/ and CLAUDE.md is empty. Every non-Sprint-31 change on the branch is exactly main's content. Sprint 30's portion of it is the commit c828bc0 I audited (PASS) as gate 1 for Sprint 30.
The sprint file is unchanged apart from its lifecycle status line. Every round-1 finding, including the R2/R6 sprint-file conflict note for Master Controller, carries over unchanged.

Re-ran these on the combined tree:
- npm test: 26 files, 291 tests, green.
- typecheck: clean.
- lint: clean.
- build: clean, /chart dynamic.
I could not run test:rls (no docker in this WSL distro). This tree now carries Sprint 30's migration as well, so CI's rls-tests job must be green in Pipeman's push report.

Note on --commit: in dev_agreed_done, /sprint-qa1 takes the gate-1 path, which hashes HEAD and ignores --commit. --commit applies only in the live loop and complete_ready. HEAD equals the requested 361d453, so the tree recorded is exactly that commit's.
commit=707e18f | ci=green: 1 CI run(s) for 707e18fe02ae5aee7434e77871de07d4e9cae07d all completed successfully with real steps executed.

PASS: PASS (round 1). Tested 2026-11-23, about 00:40 UTC, against
https://my-little-racoon.vercel.app.
Shipped commit 707e18f. Production serves the pushed tip 604d6f1: /api/health/db reports
status ok and commit 604d6f1. git diff --stat 707e18f 604d6f1 touches only
docs/sprints/state/sprint-30.json and sprint-31.json.
Tools: headless Chromium (Playwright 1.57, real navigation and clicks), curl, the anon RPC
(the user-supplied publishable key) to look up reading ids, and the gh API for job logs.

CI: runs 45040958347 (707e18f) and 45041473191 (604d6f1). build, rls-tests and migrate all
succeed in both.
- build: "Tests 291 passed (291)".
- rls-tests: "Test Files 5 passed (5)" and "Tests 43 passed (43)".
- migrate: "Remote database is up to date." and "No drift detected.".
- Both rls-tests jobs logged Docker "error from registry: Rate exceeded" while pulling images,
  and the migrate drift step logged "Data limit exceeded". These were retried within the same
  step, then "Started supabase local development setup." and the suites ran. They are
  transient registry throttling, not a defect, but worth knowing if a future run fails there.

STEP 1, /chart: PASS. curl gives 307, location https://my-little-racoon.vercel.app/ and
cache-control "public, max-age=0, must-revalidate". In the browser the chain is 307 /chart,
then 307 /, then 200 /date/2026-11-23 (h1 "23 November 2026", today in UTC). It is not a 308.

STEP 2, dated /chart: PASS. All are 307:
- /chart?date=1969-07-20 goes to /date/1969-07-20, which renders in the browser with h1
  "20 July 1969".
- /chart?date=garbage and /chart?date=2200-01-01 go to /, then to /date/2026-11-23.
- Extra cases: 1700-01-01 goes to /date/1700-01-01 and 2100-12-31 to /date/2100-12-31 (both
  boundaries are kept). 1699-12-31 and 2026-02-30 go to /. A repeated date param
  (?date=1969-07-20&date=2000-01-01) goes to /.
- Observation, not a defect: /chart/ with a trailing slash returns 308 to /chart. That is
  Next.js's own trailing-slash normalisation, and its target is /chart itself, which then
  307s. The cacheable hop never fixes a destination date page.

STEP 3, /reading/[id]: PASS, with one note about the sprint file's example id.
- The example 5bf3a1f5-b47f-4dfa-9a42-41f18eb24861, and 047e8dbd-..., are both UNWRITTEN
  readings: "The reading / NOT WRITTEN YET" with a "WRITE THE HOROSCOPE" button.
  - Each returns 200, with no step indicator (no nav or ol element) and no old-flow copy.
  - Each has no internal link at all; the only link is the Wikipedia "source".
  - That is the unchanged unwritten state. The pre-sprint panel only ever rendered the "Cast
    a new chart" link in the written state. Prod's older deployments are behind Vercel login
    (302), so this baseline comes from the git history, not a live before/after.
  - R3 requires that "Write the horoscope" for old unwritten readings stays, and it does.
  - So the example id can't show a back link by design. I tested the link on written
    readings instead.
- Written readings, with ids taken from get_reading_by_date via the anon key:
  - 0b01c79f-73d5-4fbc-afeb-d65da32ae38d (20 July 1969): 200, no step indicator. Its visible
    links are "source" and "GO TO THIS DATE" pointing at /date/1969-07-20. The HTML carries
    two anchors, a desktopOnly one and a mobile one, both href /date/1969-07-20.
  - 586064b5-6d6b-47ee-80c0-92a1a1e0c70c (15 June 2050): "GO TO THIS DATE" points at
    /date/2050-06-15.
  - Clicking "GO TO THIS DATE" on the 1969 reading landed on /date/1969-07-20, h1 "20 July
    1969".
- No visible text on any of the four reading pages matched "step N", a "1. ", "2. " or "3. "
  label, "cast a new chart", "cast the chart", "save this reading" or "see the full reading".
- /reading/abc and /reading/00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000000 both return 404 "This page
  could not be found.", so the 404 uniformity holds.

STEP 4, date page unchanged: PASS. /date/1900-01-01, 1984-02-29 and 2001-09-11 show
prev/next, the recent list (the same 11 dates in the same order) and "this exact date" /
"other years" identical to my Sprint 30 run. The current date is still marked on 2001-09-11.
The site meta description is now "Pick a date to see the sky over it and what happened that
day, and have a horoscope written for it."

STEP 5, no old-flow copy reachable from /: PASS. A breadth-first crawl to depth 2 of every
same-origin link from / reached 12 pages: / and 11 date pages. None had visible text
matching the step or old-flow patterns, and none landed on a /chart page.

STEP 6, 390px: PASS. isMobile at 390x844 on /reading/0b01c79f-... (written),
/reading/5bf3a1f5-... (unwritten) and /date/1969-07-20. scrollWidth is 390 on each, with no
element extending past 390px.

Console: the only errors are the expected 404 resource loads on the two 404 probes.
Not verified live: error.tsx's link to / needs a database outage to render, so R4 rests on
QA1's static read.
